terra.problem: The passage does not say the long walk ends at Kadesh-barnea. It later tells of further travel.
Looking for his shoes suggests Papa Dorin has feet, conflicting with his gold base.
The passage does not say Moses was worried. That feeling needs to be marked as Papa Dorin's guess.
The snack breaks the food rule: cookies are the only food allowed in comparisons unless an exception applies.
“Nobody packs a pen” adds an invented detail to the Bible event.
The text says the scouts carried fruit back, but does not say it was the only thing they carried.
The passage does not say who received the report, so “Nobody gets left out of the report” adds a detail.
The text does not say the group was small enough to travel together.
The text names the fruit they carried back, but does not say they carried no weapons.
The people do go up into the hill country later in the passage, so saying they do not go up “at all” is inaccurate.
“Moses tells it straight so they hear it again” gives a reason for his retelling that the text does not give.
“A report built to make hearts melt” assigns an intention to the report that the text does not state.
The claim about what a father carrying his son is thinking adds to Moses' comparison.
The passage does not give the father's reason for carrying his son. The explanation adds a motive to the comparison.
The passage says the LORD showed them the road, but does not say nobody ever had to guess where to go.
The five-star review makes the LORD's care and guidance the subject of a joke.
“Not when it was easy” adds a detail about Caleb's circumstances that this passage does not give.
The passage tells Moses to encourage Joshua; it does not say here that Moses did so or describe it as how he finished a season.
The passage says Joshua will enter and enable Israel to inherit the land. It does not say he will lead them in.
“Not the order they were hoping for” assigns the people a feeling the text does not give.
Calling Egypt “home” and describing the road as long add details not given in this order.
The text does not say the change happened in a short time.
The passage does not say that nothing about the hill country had changed.
The warning concerns this fight. “A fight without Him goes badly” turns it into a general claim beyond what the passage states.
“The warning got through” asserts that the people understood it. The text says Moses spoke and they would not listen.
The passage does not say whether Moses went with the people or led them. “On their own” and “Moses wasn't leading that charge” add those details.
